title: Mechanisms underlying disease-causing variants in promoters and enhancers.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record (PMID 42711518): publication type is 'Review', authors Long HK, Wu K, Barkham RS, Bickmore WA; not open access, no PMCID, no supplement flag, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links to GEO/SRA/BioProject. Zenodo DOI search returned 0 records. No data file exists to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: the review discusses an 'expanding catalog' of small noncoding monogenic disease variants in promoters, enhancers and silencers. Whether the article contains a tabulated variant list, and how many rows, is unknown; full text is paywalled and was not scraped.

a1_downloadable.note: Review article with no deposited dataset: Europe PMC shows no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links; Zenodo DOI search empty. Any variant table sits behind the publisher paywall.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table seen. A pathogenic-versus-benign label would have to be assembled from the review's cited cases plus a benign set from elsewhere, i.e. constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked: no files. Variants in a review would be listed as citations or coordinates, needing genome lookups.

a5_enough_rows.note: Row count unknown. The abstract itself says there are 'so few concrete examples' of noncoding monogenic variants, likely well under 1,500.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Any catalog from a review would be a small table.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not checked in files; per abstract, labels would be literature-curated disease associations, not model output.

existing_models.name: NCBoost (gradient-boosted classifier of pathogenic noncoding Mendelian variants, Genome Biology 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 737 curated pathogenic noncoding Mendelian variants with tenfold cross-validation; exact score not retrieved.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome (DNA sequence model) would be the natural fit if a variant table existed
backbone.hardware: CPU for scoring a few hundred variants

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not writable without a variant table; this review provides none in open form.

honest_claim_h3: No claim possible: the paper is a paywalled review with no deposited data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence around rare inherited regulatory mutations to predict whether a mutation causes disease and whether it breaks or creates gene control.
plain_idea.train_on: Small disease-causing mutations in gene control regions (promoters, enhancers) listed in the review; count unknown, likely only tens to hundreds.
plain_idea.predict: Disease-causing versus harmless, and loss versus gain of regulatory function, with answers taken from published patient genetics and lab assays cited by the review.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinical geneticists struggle to interpret noncoding mutations in rare-disease patients; a validated predictor would help, but this review does not supply the data to build one.

ml_idea: Benchmark sequence models on literature-curated noncoding Mendelian variants; not feasible from this source since no open table exists.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data to load.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the review has any supplementary variant table in an open repository; Europe PMC and Zenodo show none, which already kills it.

verdict_reason: Paywalled Nature Genetics review with no deposited data, supplement, or accessions (A1 fail); any variant catalog would be small (the abstract stresses few concrete examples) and labels would need constructing (A2).
